title: Wanhua Heritage Walk: Ximen to Longshan Temple
excerpt: A 3km self-guided walk through Wanhua, from the Red House and the Lane 50 food alley in Ximending to Bopiliao, Longshan Temple and Huaxi Street Night Market.
content:
Wanhua is the oldest district in Taipei, and this route joins its two halves: the neon and street food of Ximending in the north, and the Qing-era streets and temples around Longshan in the south. It begins at Ximen MRT, calls at the Red House and the Lane 50 food alley, then heads down Kangding Road to the Bopiliao Historical Block, Longshan Temple and Huaxi Street Night Market. Allow about 3km on foot and 3 to 4 hours with stops.

Go on any day from Tuesday to Sunday and set off in the early afternoon. Both the Red House and Bopiliao are shut on Mondays, and an afternoon start brings you to the temple around dusk, just as the night market opens up.

The Route

If you want to stay at the start of the route, the Ximending hotel guide gives the closest MRT exit for every pick.

Step-By-Step

  • 1 Take the blue or green line to Ximen and leave by exit 1
    • The Red House is the octagonal brick building just to the west of the exit
    • Exit 6, a few steps north, is the one for the main pedestrian streets of Ximending if you want to look around first
  • 2 Look inside the Red House
    • Built in 1908 under Japanese rule as a market hall, later used as a cinema and theatre
    • Inside are two floors of craft and gift stalls, a tea house and a small live music venue
    • Open Tuesday to Sunday 11:00 to 21:30 (until 22:00 on Fridays and Saturdays), closed on Mondays, and free to enter
    • The bars of the Ximen outdoor drinking area are directly behind it, but they only get going in the evening, so save them for another night
  • Walk north up Xining South Road and turn right into Wuchang Street, the pedestrianised road lined with cinemas
  • 3 Turn right again into the Lane 50 food alley (Lane 50, Section 2, Wuchang Street) and work your way south through it to Emei Street
    • Around twenty snack stalls line this short pedestrian lane, and most of them are trading by mid-afternoon
    • Look out for the torched beef cubes at the Emei Street end, the cheese tteokbokki counter next to it and Prince Cheese Potatoes
    • Don't confuse it with Lane 50 of Xining South Road, a separate lane a block to the west where Modern Toilet is
    • [optional] Ay Chung Flour Rice Noodles is two minutes east along Emei Street
  • Head west along Emei Street to Kangding Road, then turn left and follow Kangding Road south for about 15 minutes, crossing Chengdu Road and Guiyang Street
  • 4 Turn left off Kangding Road into the Bopiliao Historical Block
    • A Qing-dynasty shopping street of red-brick shophouses, saved from redevelopment because the land was set aside for a school in 1941
    • The street is open Tuesday to Sunday from 09:00 to 21:00, and the indoor exhibition rooms close at 18:00
    • At the Guangzhou Street end is the Heritage and Culture Education Center, open Tuesday to Sunday 09:00 to 17:00, with displays on the history of the area
    • Everything here is free, and everything is closed on Mondays
  • Come out onto Guangzhou Street and walk west for about five minutes
  • 5 Visit Longshan Temple
    • Guanyin, the Goddess of Mercy, has been worshipped here since Fujianese migrants built the first temple in 1738, and it remains busy with worshippers all day
    • Free, and open daily from 06:00 until 22:00, although the gates stop admitting visitors at 21:45
    • Walk through the front hall, the main hall and the rear hall in that order, and look up at the roofs
    • Visitors no longer burn incense here; people pray with their hands instead
    • [optional] Herb Lane, on Xichang Street just east of the temple, has sold medicinal herbs to temple-goers for generations
    • Bangka Park, across Guangzhou Street, reopened on 17 October 2026 after a refurbishment
  • Leave by the front gate and carry on west along Guangzhou Street for two or three minutes
  • 6 Walk north through Huaxi Street Night Market from its gateway on Guangzhou Street
    • Most of the street is covered, so it works in the rain
    • It was once known as Snake Alley, though the snake shops have all gone
    • The Taipei tourism office lists it as open daily from 16:00 to midnight
    • Some stalls don't show prices, so ask before you order

Where to Eat

  • Lane 50 is the place to graze at the start of the walk. The stalls sell one or two things each, so it's easy to try a few
  • Ay Chung serves a single dish, flour rice noodles with pig intestine, and there are no seats, so you stand and eat on the pavement
  • Yuan Fang Guabao, towards the northern end of Huaxi Street, has a Michelin Bib Gourmand for its pork belly buns. It keeps daytime hours, roughly 11:30 to 20:00, and is closed on Mondays, so get there before it shuts
  • Shaved Ice Huaxi, close to the temple end of the market, has been serving shaved ice for about a century
  • Yi Jia Zi, at No. 79 Kangding Road, is on the way down to Bopiliao and is known for braised pork belly rice; it and Wang's Broth in Huaxi Street both appear in our guide to Michelin Bib Gourmand small eats

Best Time to Go

Any day from Tuesday to Sunday will work. On Mondays the Red House, the Bopiliao Historical Block, the Heritage and Culture Education Center and Yuan Fang Guabao are all closed, which takes most of the substance out of the route.

Start at Ximen at around 14:00. The Red House will already be open, the Lane 50 stalls will be serving, you'll reach Bopiliao before its indoor rooms close, and Longshan Temple and Huaxi Street come around dusk, when the temple is lit up and the market is open.

Weekdays are calmer in Ximending, which is at its busiest on Friday and Saturday evenings. If you'd like to hear the chanting at Longshan, the reliable sessions are at 06:00 and 08:00; there is also a late-afternoon session, but published times for it vary between about 15:45 and 17:00. Taipei's city-run venues shut on typhoon days, as the Heritage and Culture Education Center did on 23 and 24 October 2026, so check the forecast in summer and autumn.

Getting There and Back

Start: Ximen station (blue and green lines), exit 1, opposite the Red House.

Finish: Longshan Temple station (blue line), one stop west of Ximen. Exit 1 is beside Bangka Park, a few minutes' walk from the Guangzhou Street end of Huaxi Street. See the MRT guide for fares and lines.

The route also works in reverse, as a morning walk: catch the 08:00 chanting at Longshan, see Bopiliao when it opens, and walk north to reach Ximending by lunchtime. Huaxi Street will be quiet at that hour, though.

Common Questions

How long is the Wanhua heritage walk?

It is about 3km from Ximen MRT to the end of Huaxi Street. With time at each stop, most people need three to four hours. The longest stretch without a stop is the 15-minute walk down Kangding Road.

Does any of it cost money?

No. The Red House, the Bopiliao Historical Block, the Heritage and Culture Education Center and Longshan Temple are all free to enter. The only spending is on food.

Can I do this walk on a Monday?

You can walk it, but the Red House and Bopiliao are both closed on Mondays. Longshan Temple and Huaxi Street Night Market are open every day, so on a Monday it's better to take the MRT straight to Longshan Temple station.

Where exactly is the Lane 50 food alley?

It is Lane 50 of Section 2, Wuchang Street, a pedestrian lane running between Wuchang Street and Emei Street in the middle of Ximending, a few minutes north of exit 6. Lane 50 of Xining South Road, home to Modern Toilet, is a different lane.

Is the area safe in the evening?

The route keeps to busy streets that are lit and full of people until late. As in any crowded market, keep an eye on your bag in Huaxi Street, and check prices before ordering at stalls that don't display them.
